title: Reliability runway snapshot and commitment playbook for SLI ownership
creator: Marina Kline
description: Goal: Build an operational artifact and lightweight dashboard that gives initiative owners and stakeholders a 30/90-day 'runway snapshot' for each reliability initiative. The runway snapshot combines current SLI attainment, error-budget burn-rate, forecasted runway (Monte Carlo and linear projections), and assigned mitigations with explicit owners. The playbook documents decision gates tied to runway thresholds (green/amber/red) and prescriptive actions (pause rollouts, increase capacity, trigger canaries). This ticket covers the PM-side orchestration: product spec, stakeholder alignment, acceptance criteria, and handoff to eng for dashboard + automation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runway snapshot view implemented in staging with per-initiative SLI and error-budget visualization; 2) Runway forecast computed using two models (linear projection + Monte Carlo) and exposed as a 30/90-day probability band; 3) Decision gate rules defined and stored as JSON spec usable by the rollout service; 4) Owner assignment and escalation flows documented; 5) Playbook published to Confluence with example runbook play and two worked scenarios; 6) Integration tests for alert triggers when runway crosses amber/red thresholds.

decisions: Use two forecasting models (linear + Monte Carlo) and surface both to give deterministic and probabilistic views.
Decision gates will be authored as a small JSON schema (threshold, window, severity, recommended action) to be consumed by rollout service.
Start with per-initiative runway snapshots (one row per initiative) rather than per-service to keep scope constrained.
Safe-mode for Dedicated customers will throttle burst capacity to a baseline instead of full rollback, per SRE recommendation.
tradeoffs: Monte Carlo gives a richer risk picture but is CPU-intensive; we will run it on a sampling cadence (every 6 hours) and offer on-demand recompute in the UI.
Per-initiative view simplifies ownership but hides cross-initiative interference; mitigation: add an 'interference' flag and link to cross-team map.
Automated rollbacks are powerful but risky; initial implementation will only produce recommended actions and an opt-in automation path for production rollouts.
